about: Where each class of a decode step's host operations may run (workflow/step_placement reads it; docs/step-placement-design-20261115.md section 1). Engine-blind: an engine's function rows name their class (data/host_functions.json `op`). device_ok: the class's work can be done on the device (or vanishes there) once every precondition holds. host_only: it must run on the host (I/O, text, streaming); it leaves the critical path only by running after the step is launched. lag_ok: a step of lag is harmless, so it may run on the host after the step (a late result is slower, not wrong). boundary: the class is the read that ends a GPU stage; it bounds a cut and is not one of its operations (the one read a step's math needs stays). scales_with: what the class's host time grows with. preconditions: what must hold before device_ok counts, each with the test that settles it; an untested precondition leaves the decision unknown, never pass.

preconditions.what: the token is chosen by argmax on the device (backend sampling on, temperature 0)
preconditions.test: the run's sampling flags: backend sampling and temperature 0

token_select.why: the draft token is already chosen on the device; reading it back to re-add it to the next pass's batch is a round trip whose inputs and consumer are both on the device (R1)

preconditions.what: the sampler chain is pure argmax: no penalties, no grammar, not the rejection-sampling variant

accept_compare.why: comparing the verify argmax with the drafts reads device outputs and feeds the next step's positions (R1, R3: per token)

preconditions.what: cache length, pool count and positions advance on the device by the accepted count; the recurrent snapshot is chosen by it (draft depth no deeper than the snapshots kept)
preconditions.test: the engine's snapshot count against the draft depth, and the device-side rollback's identity check

kv_rollback.why: rejected cells need not be erased, only overwritten later: a position counter on the device replaces the host walk (R1, R3)

preconditions.what: every input the host builds per forward is a function of device state (positions, counts, the accepted tokens)
preconditions.test: the engine's input builders, one by one, against a device-built copy (bit-identical inputs)

step_inputs.why: per-forward inputs built on the host and uploaded cost a copy and a launch on the path; built on the device they cost a small kernel in the graph (R2)

preconditions.what: the graph is shape-invariant: every kernel whose size follows the cache length reads it from a device scalar, or runs at the maximum
preconditions.test: the capture's graph rebuilds and instantiations per step after the change: zero

graph_build.why: a graph built, allocated, updated or re-instantiated because a count changed is host work that vanishes once the counts live on the device (R3: per step); launching the built graphs is graph_launch

graph_launch.scales_with: graph splits per forward: one launch per split's graph (more when a split's graph is cut into 512-node chunks); its change rate is per forward, every step

preconditions.what: the step's splits merge into one graph: no host cut between them (the expert cache's per-layer slot lookups on the device, or every expert resident)
preconditions.test: the capture's cudaGraphLaunch calls per forward after the change: one per graph chunk of a single split

graph_launch.why: launching a forward's graphs is host time on the path, one launch per split (boltbeam-runs/graph-reuse-20261116: about 31 cudaGraphLaunch a step at 33-39 us each behind the expert cache's per-layer splits); it shrinks only with the split count, and one launch per graph stays (R2, R3: per forward)

bookkeeping.why: batch and cache bookkeeping, stats and the accepted-token record are O(accepted) host work whose consumer is the host; after the step's one read they need not hold the next launch (R3, R5)

preconditions.what: the slot table lives on the device and the expert kernel reads a slot or a mapped host address
preconditions.test: the generated expert kernel bit-identical to the engine's at the step's shapes (the hook's check mode)

preconditions.what: or every expert is resident (no cache)
preconditions.test: the memory plan on the run's flags: a load probe with no host expert layers

expert_slot_lookup.why: the routed ids are on the device and the expert kernel consumes the slot: a read-back, a sync and a slot-map upload per host layer is a round trip with both ends on the device (R1, R3)

preconditions.what: the host experts are registered as mapped pinned memory, so a kernel can read a missing expert in place
preconditions.test: a load probe registering the host expert tensors: resident set, time, failure

expert_fetch.why: a miss read through a mapped address needs no host-issued copy on the path; the fill into a slot for later steps runs on a copy stream (R1)

sync_read.why: the read that ends a GPU stage: it bounds a cut. One per step stays (the accepted tokens out, R4); the others go with the cuts they bound

preconditions.what: the next step is launched before this one's text is streamed (launch-ahead)
preconditions.test: the engine's loop order in a capture: the next launch precedes this work

detokenize_stream.why: text, stop checks and the network are host work (R4); they leave the path only by running after the next launch
